🧠 Interpretation

  • σ_R shrinks from 0.0846 → 0.0147 over training — gradient signal dominates early and decays as the model converges.
  • σ_R² plateau at 0.00026 gives the curvature noise floor: tr(H²) ≈ 1.013e+08.
  • d_gradient ≈ 54,679 (0.001% of total) — these are the only dimensions being actively steered. The remaining ~100.0% are essentially inert random walk.
  • SNR drops from ~0.75 (early) to ~0.16 (late) — consistent with ZScoreES entering the curvature-dominated regime near convergence.
  • d_ratio ≈ 1 for most parameters — delta_norm_sq grows linearly as expected for a random walk, with modest excess for gradient-active directions. The excess is very small relative to total dims.

📝 Null / Negative Findings

  • The increment analysis may show near-zero growing slopes for most params — indicating that, despite a measurable d_gradient, the per-step gradient signal is very small relative to random walk noise per individual parameter.
  • The two independent |∇f|² estimates (from σ_R² and from dμ_R/dt) may disagree in the late phase — this would indicate the late-stage σ_R is dominated by curvature noise, not gradient signal, consistent with theory.
  • If d_ratio ≈ 1 uniformly across all layers/kinds, it would imply that ES is not concentrating updates in any particular layer — unlike GRPO which is expected to show layer-dependent gradients.
